system.name: Kepler-16
system.description: A binary star system 245 light-years away hosting the first confirmed circumbinary planet — a Saturn-sized world orbiting both stars, earning the nickname 'Tatooine'.

kepler16a.name: Kepler-16A
kepler16a.description: An orange K-type main-sequence star slightly smaller and cooler than the Sun. It forms a tight binary with Kepler-16B, and together they host the iconic circumbinary planet Kepler-16(AB)b.
kepler16a.funFact: Kepler-16A is so cool that it hosts a strong star-spot cycle, making it dimmer than a typical Sun-like star.

kepler16b.name: Kepler-16B
kepler16b.description: A small M-type red dwarf star that orbits Kepler-16A every 41 days at a separation of about 0.22 AU. Its much lower mass shifts the binary barycenter noticeably toward Kepler-16A.
kepler16b.funFact: Kepler-16B is so small and cool it sits right at the boundary between a very-low-mass star and a brown dwarf.

kepler16-planet.name: Kepler-16(AB)b
kepler16-planet.description: The first confirmed circumbinary planet — it orbits both Kepler-16A and B in a near-circular path every 229 days. With two suns in its sky, it inspired the nickname 'Tatooine' after the Star Wars world.
kepler16-planet.funFact: Sunsets on Kepler-16(AB)b would show two suns setting at different times, just like Tatooine in Star Wars — and this world is real.
